question: At a meeting of the Regional Technical Committee (CTR), the Maritime Authority of Brindisi has given clearance for gas carrier vessels undertaking commercial operations to moor at the as-yet-unfinished Edison LNG depot on the Costa Morena Est quay in the port of Brindisi.
In note No 15178 of 30 July 2021, the Maritime Authority issued a second opinion to the Ministry of Ecological Transition’s Directorate-General for Environmental Restoration.

The Maritime Authority has failed, however, to address the issue of 'safety rules for the mooring of vessels that transport dangerous goods’ as it is obliged to do under Order No 16/1974 of the Brindisi Harbour Master's Office, which does not currently allow gas carrier vessels to moor on the Costa Morena Est quay.
These are prohibited because of the quay’s lack of fire-fighting facilities and its proximity to docking berths for passenger and goods vessels1. Can the Commission therefore say: 1.
Whether it intends to have the European Maritime Safety Agency carry out an inspection of installations at the port of Brindisi, pursuant to Article 9(4) of Regulation (EC) No 725/2004?
Whether it intends to check whether Italy has provided the information required under Article 4 of Regulation (EC) No 725/2004 for installations at the port of Brindisi?
answer: The Commission carries out inspections in Member States’ ports, to verify the implementation of EU maritime security legislation (2). In this regard, the Commission regularly carries out inspections in Italy. However, for security reasons, the Commission cannot disclose where it will carry out maritime security inspections in the future.

The Commission regularly verifies the information required under Article 4 of Regulation (EC) No 725/2004, both based on the reporting done by Member States and through port inspections. At the same time, the Commission recalls that it is also for national authorities to carry out administrative and control tasks relating to these security measures.

These authorities may be in a position to provide more information to the Honourable Member. The Commission would like to highlight that the main purpose of Regulation (EC) No 725/2004 is to protect port facilities and ships against threats of intentional unlawful acts, in particular acts of terrorism.
It does not address, for example, the issue of ‘safety rules for the mooring of vessels that transport dangerous goods’ that is raised in the question, and which is a national competence.
